titel: Hotel near Hertog Jan Brouwerij | Hotel Asteria Venray
omschrijving: Hertog Jan Brouwerij in Arcen is a 23-minute drive from Hotel Asteria in Venray. A guided tour with tasting, then wellness and dinner at the hotel.
hero-sub: A guided tour of the brewery in Arcen, from the hops to the tasting glass. A 23-minute drive from your hotel room in Venray.
hero-alt: The white buildings of Hertog Jan Brouwerij in Arcen with flags and the reception
t3-waarde: Wed to Sun, 11 am to 5 pm (Nov to Apr)
v1-p1: Hertog Jan brews its beer in Arcen, close to the river Maas. From Hotel Asteria it is a 23-minute drive. On the tour a guide takes you through the old brewery building and the whole brewing process: you smell the hops, taste the malt and finish with the beer itself.
v1-p2: You pass the copper brewing kettles and end up in a cellar with bottles of Grand Prestige from different vintages. A tour takes about an hour and is in Dutch. Would you prefer a tour in English or German? Ask the brewery in advance.
v1-alt: A glass and a bottle of Hertog Jan Winterbier on a bar
v2-p1: If you want to see more, book the Liefhebbers Tour (the beer lovers' tour). In about two and a half hours you go where the regular tour does not: the Grand Prestige maturing cellar, the story behind the barrel-aged Vatgerijpt beers and the pilot brewery. The tour takes sixteen people at most and is for over-18s only.
v2-p2: Once a year there is also a day devoted to Grand Prestige, with special tours and tastings. The brewery announces the dates in its newsletter and on social media.
v2-alt: Two stoneware jugs from the Arcense Stoombierbrouwerij next to bottles of Hertog Jan Dubbel, Tripel and Grand Prestige
v3-p1: Across the road from the brewery is Café de Hertog Jan Proeverij. Its lager comes straight from the brewery through a beer pipe under the road, and there are some 125 speciality beers to choose from. You can have lunch, drinks or dinner there and book up to 90 days ahead. In summer, combine your visit with the castle gardens, Kasteeltuinen Arcen, a four-minute drive away. They are closed in winter and reopen at the end of March.
v3-alt: Red Japanese gate by the pond in Kasteeltuinen Arcen
tip: Book the tour around midday and reserve a table for lunch at the Proeverij across the road afterwards. Decide before you set off who is driving back to Venray; they skip the beer that day. And note: in winter the brewery is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays.
g1-tekst: That is the pattern from November to April. Thursday and Sunday for tours only.
g1-alt: The Hertog Jan brewery building in Arcen with two flags
g2-tekst: On brouwerij.hertogjan.nl. A tour goes ahead with at least six people in total.
g2-alt: Sacks of malt on a pallet at Hertog Jan Brouwerij
g3-tekst: No cash. You pay by debit card or credit card (Visa or Mastercard).
g3-ico: <rect x='3' y='6' width='18' height='12' rx='2'/><path d='M3 10h18'/><path d='M7 15h4'/>
g3-alt: A stoneware jug from the Arcense Stoombierbrouwerij with a numbered Grand Prestige certificate
g4-tekst: Narrow, low corridors. No walkers, pushchairs, wheelchairs or dogs; guide dogs are welcome.
g4-alt: A row of bottles of Hertog Jan Grand Prestige, Pilsener and Speciaal Bier on a shelf
dag-sub: Breakfast at the hotel, the brewery in Arcen around midday and back in the late afternoon for the sauna and dinner.
m1-tekst: The breakfast buffet is served from 7 to 10 am on weekdays and from 8 to 10.30 am at weekends. Then it is a 23-minute drive to Arcen.
m1-alt: Basket of fresh bread rolls on the breakfast buffet at Hotel Asteria in Venray
m2-tekst: An hour's tour with tasting, then the brewery shop and lunch at the Proeverij across the road. Whoever is driving back leaves the beer.
m2-alt: Two horizontal stainless steel tanks at Hertog Jan Brouwerij
m3-tekst: Back in Venray, unwind in the sauna. The wellness area is open Monday to Thursday from 4 to 10 pm and Friday to Sunday from 12 noon to 10 pm. Tuesday is swimwear day.
m3-alt: Foot bath with green mosaic tiles under a skylight in the Top Floor wellness area at Hotel Asteria
m4-tekst: The day ends at the table in the hotel brasserie. The kitchen is open until 9.30 pm, and afterwards your room is just a lift ride away.
m4-alt: Bartender pulling a beer at the brasserie bar in Hotel Asteria, Venray
kamers-sub: After a day in Arcen there is nowhere else you need to be. Choose your room; you will see the price for your dates as soon as you book.
kaart-regel: The brewery is in Arcen on the river Maas, south-east of Venray. The map also shows three other days out near the hotel.
kaart-naam: Hertog Jan Brouwerij, Kruisweg 44, 5944 EN Arcen
kaart-alt: Map of North Limburg with Hotel Asteria in Venray, Hertog Jan Brouwerij in Arcen and three other days out
f1-v: How far is Hertog Jan Brouwerij from Hotel Asteria?
f1-a: It is 20.5 kilometres, about 23 minutes by car. By bike it is 16.3 kilometres, around 70 minutes; you can hire bikes at our reception. Because of roadworks on Kruisweg and Maasstraat there is currently a diversion: if you are driving, follow the B signs.
f2-v: How long does a tour take, and in which language?
f2-a: About an hour. Afterwards you can visit the brewery shop and the Hertog Jan Proeverij. Tours are in Dutch; for a tour in English or German, please ask the brewery in advance. The Liefhebbers Tour takes around two and a half hours and is for over-18s only.
f3-v: Do I need to book the tour in advance?
f3-a: The brewery strongly recommends it; you book on brouwerij.hertogjan.nl. A tour costs €19.95 for adults and €9.95 for young people aged 12 to 17; children under 12 go free when accompanied. These are the prices as of November 2026. Payment is by debit or credit card only.
f4-v: Is the brewery a good day out when it rains?
f4-a: Yes, the tour is indoors. Do check the day, though: from November to April the brewery is open on Wednesday, Friday and Saturday from 11 am to 5 pm, and on Thursday and Sunday for tours only. It is closed on Monday and Tuesday; during the Dutch school holidays it is also open on Tuesday.
f5-v: Can I bring my dog to the brewery?
f5-a: No, only guide dogs are allowed. Bear in mind too that you walk through narrow, low corridors and climb 144 steps; walkers, pushchairs and wheelchairs cannot come along.
f6-v: Can I still use the wellness area and have dinner at the hotel after the brewery?
f6-a: Yes. The wellness area is open Monday to Thursday from 4 to 10 pm and Friday to Sunday from 12 noon to 10 pm. Tuesday is swimwear day. Dinner in the brasserie is served until 9.30 pm. If you have been drinking at the tasting, let someone who has not do the driving. Parking at Hotel Asteria is free.

arcen.desc: A four-minute drive from the brewery are the castle gardens of Arcen: more than fifteen gardens around a 17th-century castle, with a rose garden, an oriental water garden and the tropical glasshouse Casa Verde. The gardens are closed in winter and reopen at the end of March.
arcen.credit: Photos: Vincent van Zeijst and Kasteeltuinen Arcen via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.

maasduinen.desc: Between Venray and Arcen lies the longest belt of river dunes in the Netherlands, with over 4,500 hectares of woodland, heath, drift sand and fens. At the visitor centre in Well you can pick a walking or cycling route. A good morning outdoors before you head to the brewery.
maasduinen.credit: Photos: Lieblingsgouda, Steven Lek, Carelbullens and Jonathation via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA), cropped.

venray.desc: The centre of Venray is about four kilometres from the hotel. On the Grote Markt stands the Sint-Petrus' Bandenkerk, known locally as the cathedral of the Peel, with a tower of almost 80 metres. Around the square you will find terraces for coffee or lunch.
venray.credit: Photos: Dosseman, giggel, WoodenSpoon and Sindala via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA and CC BY), cropped.
